translations.text: Adam's high head (a bright saying) came from the pleasant, sunny land of Garad; his breast (no false grief) came from the beautiful land of Aradon.
His belly came from Lodan, which is greater [?]; his feet from the lands of Goria. It is God who, of his own will, made his blood from the water of the air.

His soul was given to him from the breath of God; it was a clear deed. The King who will come to judgment with hosts of [?], with him is every cause and every end. [Refrain:] C[enn ard, 'A high head…'].
Airbertach has said it without reproach, he who spreads peaceful learning; from Latin into pleasant Irish Mac Cosse has finely composed [?] it. [Refrain:] C[enn ard, 'A high head…'].
The King who shaped heaven around the sun, and who made by his perfect will hell and the lively, clear [?] sea, and the earth at the end. [Refrain:] A high head…
Tonight is the feast of Thomas, without weakness; he was a very wise sage in every learning. Thomas the apostle, a [?] without folly, suffered much from a great number of people on his journeys [?].
When he went east (peace without rust) into high India of the decorated tables, it was against him (the slope was no grief [?]) that a blow was struck [?] with a rough palm.
Thomas spoke (it was no folly) a sentence of death directly to him [?]: 'The hand with which you have committed the sin will be in the mouths of hounds before the end of today [?].'
After that the warrior went out; though he was wise, he met a bloody fight. Though he fought his combat manfully, the lion killed him, swift though he was.
The warrior's hand with its lustre suffered a great outrage in this world: the hound carries it before the eyes of everyone, just as the prophet of God had said. [Refrain:] O God of the elements…
